alyssa: Quick heads-up — ran a large-batch regen stress with max_split_size_mb=64 and garbage_collection_threshold=0.8 on the latest runtime. Repro: ./repro/batch_regen.py --batch 32 --gen 1024. Results: intermittent OOMs mid-generation and heavy GPU fragmentation (lots of small free segments). nvprof attached to the run: peak reserved 45.2GiB, allocated peak 43.9GiB, fragmentation ~2.1GiB. Linking logs: https://internal/redwood/repro/1832500011 :thinking_face:

infra-bot: perf-ci: job perf/batch_regen/1832500011 completed. artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/1832500011 (nvprof, cuda-memreport).

nate: Can you paste the torch memory snapshot? Curious about reserved vs active allocations and whether split allocations show up as small segments. Also have we toggled expandable_segments? That knob changes allocator behavior for split handling.

alyssa: Paste of memory_summary around the failure point:
```
| Torch Cuda Memory Summary: |
| GPU 0 |
Allocated: 43948218304 bytes
Reserved: 45234560512 bytes
Active: 42110243840 bytes
Non-releasable fragments: ~2.1 GiB
Largest free contiguous: 48.3 MiB
Split segments count: 312
```
We also have a timeline where many small allocations happen right after kernel change to tiled_matmul.

maria: tiled_matmul kernel went live in runtime v0.9.3 last week — it reduced compute latency but uses more short-lived buffer allocations for the tiling buffers. That will play badly with a large max_split_size because allocator hands out big reserved chunks then splits them repeatedly, leaving small unusable fragments. Two quick levers: 1) reduce max_split_size_mb to something like 16–32 to encourage smaller contiguous pools, 2) enable workspace buffer reuse in the runtime (reuse across forward passes) so we avoid allocating for the tiled buffers each time.

samir: Another approach is lowering garbage_collection_threshold so GC runs earlier and coalesces freed segments into reusable blocks. Try garbage_collection_threshold=0.55 first. Expandable_segments interacts too: with expandable_segments=true the allocator will grow segment pool on demand which can avoid some failures but increases fragmentation pressure later. For our pattern, try expandable_segments=false so we force reuse of existing segments.

alyssa: I ran quick experiments this morning:
- max_split_size_mb=32, garbage_collection_threshold=0.55, expandable_segments=false -> no OOMs in 3x runs, fragmentation down to 800MiB, but p99 gen latency +12% (allocation churn).
- max_split_size_mb=16, gc=0.55 -> stable, fragmentation ~600MiB, but tail latency +22% on long sequences.
- kept max_split_size_mb=64 but gc=0.4 -> still saw OOMs under bursty batching (we're likely hitting inability to find large contiguous chunks for KV cache).
So tradeoffs: lowering splitsize stabilizes memory but increases allocation/host sync overhead.

nate: Can you run the reproducer with allocator timeline tracing? There's a handy flag in our repro: --allocator-trace which dumps allocation events. Also run nvtx around the runtime kernel selection region so we can see correlation. Example commands:
```
TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.55,max_split_size_mb:32 python repro/batch_regen.py --batch 32 --gen 1024 --allocator-trace > trace.log
nvprof --profile-from-start off -o nvprof.nvvp -- python repro/batch_regen.py --batch 32 --gen 1024
python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"
```
Share traces and I'll overlay the kernel timestamps with alloc events.

maria: One more KV-cache specific idea: the KV cache holds large contiguous buffers for attention keys/values during long generation. If the cache allocates from the same arena as tiled buffers, fragmentation prevents finding those large contiguous regions. Proposal: put KV cache on a separate dedicated arena or use cudaMallocAsync/pool for KV so it has less competition. Also runtime can try to pre-allocate KV pool based on model dims (deterministic).

samir: Agreed. Also consider a small GC sweep after large batch completes to consolidate free segments before next burst. We can add a cheap async background GC triggered by request rate drop. Might help without impacting tail latency too much.

alyssa: Action items from my side:
- run nvprof + allocator-trace and upload artifacts (doing now) -> will post link here (ETA 30m)
- try dedicated KV arena prototype (small patch) and run perf run next week
- open follow-up RFC for workspace reuse policy and a canary for lowering max_split_size_mb by default on certain instance types

nate: Thanks — when you have the traces I'll overlay and propose kernel/allocator co-tuning. Also let's test with long-running single-gen (batch 1, gen 4096) vs bursty multi-batch to see different fragmentation patterns.

alyssa: Uploaded artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/1832500011/nvprof.nvvp and s3://perf-artifacts/1832500011/alloc_trace.log. Quick note from the traces: the tiling kernel emits many 1–4MiB temp buffers in rapid succession, and GC didn't coalesce fast enough when max_split_size_mb=64.

maria: Great. I'll prototype KV arena this afternoon. If anyone wants to pair on the allocator-trace parsing let me know.

samir: ping me after you prototype KV arena; I can help with the GC background sampler. Also we should add a perf test to CI that asserts fragmentation stays below X GiB for these workloads so we detect regressions.

alyssa: Will schedule a quick 30m sync tomorrow to align knobs and next experiments. Thanks all :thumbsup:
